title: Python import resolver + pipeline wiring
description:
Create the Python import resolver and wire it into the pipeline. This is the most algorithmically complex piece — package root discovery via __init__.py scanning, absolute import resolution, relative import resolution with level-based directory walk.

Covers plan Steps 6-7 from sutra/116.

acceptance_criteria.text: src/python_imports.rs created with resolve_python_imports(db, workspace_root) -> Result<usize>
Package root discovery: scans indexed __init__.py files to build package tree, finds topmost package dirs, their parents are roots
.sutra/rules.toml [python] package_roots override supported for src-layout projects
Absolute import resolution: splits module path on '.', tries {root}/{segments}.py then {root}/{segments}/__init__.py for each package root
Relative import resolution: counts leading dots for level, walks up from importing file's dir, resolves remaining module path
Db::unresolved_python_imports() query added (or reuse unresolved_imports_with_files with language filter)
Wired into post_parse_sequence in src/pipeline.rs after C resolver block
pub mod python_imports added to src/lib.rs

Tests: absolute resolution (foo.bar → foo/bar.py), package resolution (foo → foo/__init__.py), relative import (from . import sibling), multi-level relative (from ..utils import helper), unresolved external stays NULL

execution_record: Straightforward implementation following the existing pattern from c_imports.rs / dart_packages.rs / rust_imports.rs. All 10 unit tests cover the acceptance criteria test cases. Progressive segment fallback added so `from foo.bar import Baz` (raw_path 'foo.bar.Baz') resolves to foo/bar.py when Baz is a name in bar, not a submodule.

messages.author: agent
messages.text: Note from sutra/187 review: collect_import_from now emits fully-qualified raw_paths (e.g. 'pathlib.Path', '.utils', '..models.User') instead of just the module name. The resolver can use these directly — no need to re-parse the AST to recover imported symbol names. Wildcard imports (from X import *) still store just the module path since there's no specific symbol.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (covers sutra/188 + sutra/189 together):

Verdict: needs-attention

Findings:
1. [high] Greedy prefix resolution can turn invalid imports into local edges (python_imports.rs:160-175) — `try_resolve_segments` walks shorter prefixes until any module/package exists. `import pkg.foo.bar` resolves to `pkg/foo.py` when it exists, even though Python requires `pkg.foo` to be a package. Impact: unresolved or external imports hidden as local dependency edges, corrupting graph/impact/constraints.
2. [medium] Auto-discovered package roots resolve nondeterministically (python_imports.rs:71-106) — HashSet→into_iter() means root ordering varies across runs. In monorepos with multiple roots containing the same package name, same import can resolve to different files.
3. [high] Unresolved Python effect fallback doesn't see real dotted calls (attributes.rs:155-162) — Python parser records attribute refs as bare identifiers (`get`), not full chains (`requests.get`). Effect pattern matching against `requests` prefix won't fire on production parser output.
